#4429. Honda Is Betting $3 Billion On Hybrids As It Pulls Back From EVs

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Honda is building a new car factory in the United States, which will primarily manufacture hybrid and traditional gas vehicles. The new facility, which is estimated to cost $3 billion, will be Honda’s fourth auto plant in Ohio and the company’s ninth car-related production facility in the U.S.

The move is part of the Japanese automaker’s push to introduce no fewer than 15 new hybrid models globally, with the majority of them being destined for the American market, too. It’s also Honda’s first big step away from its ill-fated electric-car push, which ended up with a completely new vehicle platform and three EVs being retired before even one production-ready unit had rolled off the assembly line.

Honda's New Manufacturing Plant Location In Ohio

As a reminder, the Acura RSX, Honda 0 Series Saloon, and Honda 0 Series SUV were supposed to go into production at a new EV hub in Ohio, but the entire plan was scrapped due to major financial losses. After canceling the 0 Series project, the company posted its first loss in nearly 70 years, with $9 billion going down the drain.

After the whole EV debacle, Honda decided to go back to the drawing board and chose ultra-efficient hybrids as its next big thing in the U.S. The car manufacturer is already knee-deep in the development of multiple hybrid models, with the first cars expected to debut in 2028.

To support the new strategy, Honda’s new plant, which is located right next to three of its other facilities in Ohio, is scheduled to become operational in 2029. According to the company, the new location will add over 2,000 jobs and will be able to manufacture 240,000 vehicles annually, raising the automaker’s total annual U.S. production capacity to 1.3 million cars. What’s more, the new Ohio plant will increase Honda’s hybrid powertrain system capacity by 250% in the state.

Honda's new Ohio auto plant location in relation to current Honda facilities

All this being said, the latest Ohio factory is being built with flexibility in mind. Despite being aimed at hybrids at first, the company said that it will be able to add EVs into the mix in the future, if needed.

Elsewhere, Honda is investing in retooling factories to support its big hybrid push. The Alabama Auto/Engine Plant, the Anna Engine Plant in Ohio, the Transmission Plant in Ohio, and the Transmission Plant in Georgia are undergoing upgrades right now, adding equipment and new lines.

Earlier this year, when the car manufacturer announced its hybrid plans, two new vehicles were brought on stage: a Honda-badged sedan and an Acura-badged crossover. Neither has been confirmed, but we do know that electric all-wheel drive will be offered as part of the next-generation hybrid powertrain, and that crossovers will make up most of the lineup.

According to the Japanese automaker, the new system is designed to deliver 10% more efficiency than the current generation that debuted in 2023.

#4428. Stolen McLaren 750S Spotted Doing Donuts at Detroit Street Takeover, Tracked Down Via Social Media

The McLaren's owner put his 1.1 million followers to work tracking down his purloined supercar.

If you’re going to steal a bright green McLaren 750S, you might want to try to keep a low profile. At least, as low a profile as can be possible in a supercar. Doing donuts at a street takeover in front of a crowd of spectators, then, is probably not the best idea.

According to ClickOnDetroit, this indeed happened. The McLaren in question belonged to Ali Sobh, a Detroit businessman and social media influencer with approximately 1.1 million followers. The exotic car was reportedly stolen from a driveway behind his home in Detroit's historic Boston-Edison neighborhood. Sobh was understandably upset when he realized his prized possession was taken; however, salt arrived in the wound when he saw a video circulating online showing his McLaren spinning donuts in front of spectators, many of whom were recording the spectacle on their phones.

So, Sobh turned to his social media followers for help locating the McLaren. Tips began coming in, eventually providing a possible location near Six Mile Road and Telegraph Road. Sobh passed that information along to Detroit police, who subsequently recovered the car.

Getting the McLaren back is obviously a big win, but that’s not the end of the story. Detroit police are reviewing footage from the street takeover and working to identify those responsible for the theft. Authorities have not announced any arrests, and it's unclear whether the person performing donuts was involved in stealing the vehicle.

Sobh claims his car is worth approximately $500,000, and he doesn’t ever want it stolen again, so he says plans to improve security around his home to prevent that from happening. In the meantime, it must be reassuring to know that he can count on more than one million followers to help him out when things go south.

#4427. BYD offices raided as JLR legal battle heats up over alleged Defender lookalike

The raid took place at BYD’s offices in the Netherlands, where bailiffs acting for Jaguar Land Rover reportedly seized documents before a court case this week over its “copycat” Defender SUV, the Ti 7.

After BYD opened orders for the Ti 7 in Europe and the UK in late July, many (including us at Electrek) compared it to the iconic Land Rover Defender, with its boxy, rugged (yet still elegant) SUV design.

BYD even described it as having “an unapologetically boxy profile” that delivers “the imposing, chunky design that finds favour among SUV buyers, yet delivers a contemporary look.”

Apparently, JLR has also taken notice. According to a report from The Times, court bailiffs acting on behalf of the British luxury automaker raided BYD’s offices in the Netherlands and seized digital records.

The raid comes ahead of a preliminary court ruling on Wednesday, which will determine whether BYD’s Ti7 SUV infringes on the intellectual property of the Land Rover Defender.

JLR believes BYD stripped down the Defender to reverse engineer some of its technology. Before the raid, BYD claims it fully cooperated with JLR’s requests.

According to local reports, BYD’s lawyers called JLR’s raid a “fishing expedition” and claimed, “too many files were seized.”

JLR declined to comment, while BYD said it had no comment at this time as it’s in an ongoing legal case.

The Ti 7 is on sale starting at £47,995 ($64,000) in the UK, on the road. That’s over £20,000 ($26,500) less than the plug-in Defender 110, which starts at £71,840 ($95,500) in the UK.

It has a seven-seat arrangement, which BYD said was specifically designed for the European and UK markets.

As the first vehicle in the UK based on its DM-p (Dual Mode performance) powertrain, BYD said the Ti 7 “vastly exceeds the closest competition,” seemingly another jab at the Defender.

"...to reverse engineer some of its technology". No doubt so their engineers would know what NOT to do.

The setup uses three electric motors and a 1.5-liter turbocharged engine, delivering a combined 402 hp (408 PS), enabling it to accelerate from 0 to 62 mph in 4.8 seconds.

The engine primarily powers a 35.6 kWh BYD Blade Battery, which provides a pure-electric WLTP driving range of up to 74 miles. In the city, it has an electric range of up to 102 miles.

Available exclusively in the UK in the flagship Excellence AWD trim, BYD claims that the Ti 7 offers “a level of equipment that exceeds anything that its rivals can offer at this price point.”

With the preliminary ruling scheduled for Wednesday, we should learn more about the BYD and JLR legal battle soon. Check back for updates as this is an ongoing story.

#4426. 2027 Chevrolet Silverado HD, a Gorilla-Strong Pickup You Don’t Have to Wrestle With

A monstrously torquey new 8.3-liter turbo-diesel V-8 and new electric power steering make this heavy-duty pickup easy to drive.

The lightest Atlas stone used in international strongman competitions is 220 pounds. The heaviest is nearly 500 pounds. Extremely large, frighteningly strong people lift these big orbs onto shoulder-high plinths, and just watching it will give you an inferiority complex—and sciatica. Luckily, there’s a way to feel a similar sense of broad-shouldered accomplishment without spending a lifetime in the gym. Drive the 2027 Chevy Silverado Heavy-Duty (HD) pickup, preferably with a trailer attached, and you’ll get the same rush of endorphins as 2026 World Strongest Man champion Mitchell Hooper as he lifted spheres and repped deadlifts of over 800 pounds.

While the 2027 Silverado 1500 got a full redesign for 2027, the HD is mostly carryover in body and interior. Still, it has some new delights, the biggest and most delightful being the new 8.3-liter Duramax V-8 turbo-diesel engine. This big brute belts out 555 horsepower and 1230 pound-feet of torque, is backed by a 10-speed automatic transmission, and makes light work of towing even the heaviest trailer.

See all results for new 2027 Chevrolet Silverado 2500HD / 3500HD for sale near 10025

To keep the burly engine happy, the HD trucks have a revised cooling system with a four-deep stack of radiators, charge coolers, and oil coolers. To keep the driver cool when stopping a fully loaded HD pickup, 14.6-inch front brake rotors clamped by four-piston calipers replace the outgoing model’s two-piston binders. An electronic brake booster, a first for a heavy-duty pickup, gives the brake pedal a similar feel to what you’d find in a regular SUV, no heavy foot needed for effective braking.

To demonstrate the diesel’s grunt, Chevy hooked up a massive trailer loaded with construction equipment and let us rip, towing nearly 37,000 pounds down a drag strip. The new trucks are rated for up to 38,000 pounds with a gooseneck trailer (when equipped with the Max Trailering package). The NHRA won’t be adding a sled-pulling class to its competition anytime soon, but the big truck moved out with barely a shudder, and the upgraded brakes and e-booster made stopping at the far end as easy as launching. The most intimidating part of the pull was making the turnout at the end of the strip, but the HD’s smooth power delivery and redesigned steering made for a drama-free turn despite the tight corner.

The 2500 HD lineup encompasses six trims, starting with the WT (Work Truck) and topping out with the optioned-up High Country. The base engine remains a 6.6-liter gas-burning V-8 (distinct from the similarly sized optional V-8 in redesigned 2027 light-duty models), albeit updated to now develop 412 horsepower and 472 pound-feet of torque. The new Duramax V-8 is an $11,400 option, and it’s available on all trims. That’s a big jump from the outgoing 6.6-liter diesel V-8, which added only $9990 to the HD’s price. Luckily for truck shoppers, overall starting prices see a smaller price hike. The MSRP for the 2027 WT begins at $49,995 (an increase of $1000 versus 2026), and the High Country now starts at $78,195.

See all results for new 2027 Chevrolet Silverado 2500HD / 3500HD for sale near 10025

Step up into the cabin—or haul yourself up with the grab handle—and you’ll find the interior is little changed from 2026 models. It’s spacious and cushy with big storage compartments, but the design and the dash layout are the same as before. What is new is some of the software available through the 13.4-inch center touchscreen. There’s an updated Tow/Haul mode that fine-tunes power delivery, shift points, and braking to make for smoother towing up and downhill. An Off-Road mode allows more wheelspin to prevent bog-downs, and off-road-oriented ZR2 HDs get the same Terrain mode as the light-duty version, a trail-focused tune that teams the throttle with automatic braking for what’s essentially one-pedal driving during off-roading. Optional camera add-ons make for up to 14 different views, including an invisible-trailer mode and a split screen when reversing. In the various camera views, the HD lacks the light duty’s helpful graphic overlays, but it’s probably fair to assume that buyers of heavy-duty trucks aren’t beginners at towing.

Another feature that has not made its way from light duty to heavy duty is Chevy’s Super Cruise hands-free driving. In the past, this was because the HD still used a hydraulic steering system, but a major change for 2027 is the switch to electric power steering. The new rack-and-pinion electric steering setup is another first for the HD, and it makes a big difference in the feedback through the wheel and consistency of steering feel even during braking and hard steering inputs. It gives the HD a more consumer-friendly feel. On a mountain road, these big rigs feel manageable, and while you still won’t want to swing a tight U-turn, there’s no fighting the wheel when changing direction. While this year’s trucks won’t offer Super Cruise, the technology is in place for GM to fit additional driver aids in the future.

That omission aside, the theme of the HDs’ changes for 2027 is ease of use. Most of what’s new isn’t visible from the outside, but it’s all designed to make the tasks of hauling and towing feel less like a job and more like a cruise in a passenger vehicle—a really burly passenger vehicle.

#4425. PlugShare Gets A Major Redesign, Adds Dark Mode And iPhone Duo Support

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

PlugShare, the smartphone app that brings together the largest community of EV drivers in the world, has been redesigned to include new features and compatibility with new devices. Version 8.0, which is now live on the Apple App Store, introduces dark mode, a redesigned user experience, and a performance boost.

It’s the first time in the app’s 15-year history that dark mode has been available, and it’s all down to the PlugShare community, which has been feverishly requesting the feature for years.

“PlugShare has always been shaped by the drivers who use it, and we remain community-driven 15 years after our first app launch,” said Corey Davis, PlugShare Senior Director, Software. “The update is a near-total rebuild of the PlugShare app. We’ve redesigned nearly every screen using Apple’s latest design language, making it feel faster, fresher, and more useful for PlugShare users.”

The latest iOS app version adds support for the new iPhone Duo and improves a few user experience items. Switching between different tabs is now instant. Furthermore, users can open and zoom into location photos directly from the image thumbnails, and trips display the exact distance from the starting point and from the previous stop.

The Apple Watch app also got some love. Users can find nearby chargers directly on their wrist, and the smartwatch automatically applies the same filters set on the smartphone app, so drivers will only see chargers that are compatible with their cars.

Tapping on a location will show its Plug Score, the charging network, the connector types, and a small preview map. The list of chargers refreshes every time the user’s wrist is raised and the app is open.

Apple’s iPad also gets a rebuilt app that adapts its layout to the tablet’s screen size.

It’s not hard to spot that the latest PlugShare app is all about Apple devices right now, but Android users will get a refreshed experience, too. The company said it’s working on shipping dark mode and a Material 3-based design in early 2027.

PlugShare claims it’s the world’s largest community of EV drivers who contribute real-time check-ins, reviews, and photos. The service debuted in 2009 and has gradually introduced solutions for charging operators and car manufacturers, in addition to the charging map available for EV drivers for free. In 2021, Recargo, the company behind PlugShare, was acquired by EVgo for $25 million.

Anyone can create an account and use the app to find chargers from all operators. Some charging networks support payment through PlugShare and manage their locations directly, but in other cases, EV drivers are the ones who keep the locations up to date.

#4424. Juiced unveils another lower-cost moto-styled electric bike: Scrambler Core

Juiced Bikes is expanding its recently relaunched Scrambler lineup with a new, more affordable model known as the Juiced Scrambler Core. The new bike keeps much of the moto-inspired styling and performance of the existing Scrambler Hardtail, but trims back several components to knock several hundred dollars off the price.

The new Scrambler Core starts at $1,399, compared to $1,699 for the existing Scrambler Hardtail.

Juiced is also offering a $1,599 long-range version of the Core, as well as a smaller “Midsize” frame that should make the bike much more accessible to shorter riders – and, perhaps more importantly, teenagers.

Teens are a major part of the moto-style e-bike market, and Juiced has designed its Scrambler e-bikes as a safer option for those younger riders. In addition to ensuring street-legal performance for most major markets, Juiced rolled out a feature known as Speed Lock, which is essentially a parental control option that lets a parent or guardian set a lower speed limit using a PIN code that prevents their teen from later modifying the speed limit.

The launch comes as part of the rebirth of Juiced Bikes following the brand’s acquisition last year. The company was founded in 2009 and was acquired in 2025 by the co-founders of Lectric Ebikes, who have since brought the brand back with a new generation of its popular Scrambler platform.

The biggest changes appear to be in the powertrain, battery, brakes, and suspension.

The standard Scrambler Hardtail launched earlier this year set the standard for the flagship models by using a 750W nominal motor with 90 Nm of torque and reaching 28 mph (45 km/h). Its 52V 19.2Ah battery provides nearly 1 kWh of capacity and a claimed range of up to 60 miles (96 km).

The Scrambler Core steps down to a 500W nominal rear hub motor rated for 1,176W peak and 80 Nm of torque. Top speed is also reduced slightly to 25 mph (40 km/h), while the throttle is limited to 20 mph (32 km/h). Importantly, though, Juiced has retained its 52V architecture, meaning this is still a fairly punchy setup rather than a dramatically detuned budget bike.

Battery capacity takes a hit as well. The standard Core gets a 52V 10Ah battery with 520 Wh of capacity, rated for up to 40 miles (64 km) of range. Spending another $200 gets the Core Long-Range with a 52V 15Ah, 780Wh battery and a claimed 60-mile (96 km) maximum range. As with nearly all e-bikes, expect real-world range to fall short of the idealized advertised numbers, which are generally only achievable under the lowest power pedal assist.

Juiced also traded the Talon P4 four-piston hydraulic brakes found on the more expensive Scrambler for Talon P2 two-piston brakes. The KKE inverted fork with 140mm of travel is gone too, replaced by a more conventional aluminum triple-crown fork with 100mm of travel.

Those are meaningful downgrades, but they’re also largely the kinds of changes I’d expect to see when trying to shave $300 off an already competitively priced moto-style e-bike. It’s a strategy we’ve seen play out before in the industry, helping lower costs for riders who want a flagship bike but don’t necessarily want to pay flagship prices.

Even so, important features remain to help maintain the look and feel of the Juiced Scrambler line. The Core still gets 20 x 4-inch fat tires, hydraulic disc brakes, a frame-integrated TFT display, four pedal-assist levels, a headlight, taillight, brake light, and turn signals. It’s a single-speed setup and weighs 73 lb (33 kg), while being rated for a 300 lb (136 kg) payload.

Perhaps the more interesting addition is the Scrambler Core Midsize.

While the regular Core is recommended for riders 5’2” and taller, the Midsize drops that figure to just 4’10”. Pricing remains the same: $1,399 with the 520Wh battery or $1,599 with the 780Wh long-range pack.

And with an eye towards safety, the Core and Core Mini retain Juiced’s PIN-protected parental speed lock. Parents can set the motor-assisted top speed anywhere from 1-25 mph and lock the setting behind a four-digit PIN. That makes even more sense on the Midsize version, which seems tailor-made for younger riders who want the moto-style look but may not yet comfortably fit the larger Scrambler.

The Core is launching in several decidedly Juiced color names, including Black Nectar, Fruit Punch, Sour Grape, White Grape, Berry Freeze, and Blood Orange, though availability varies between frame sizes and battery configurations. Juiced says preorders are expected to begin shipping around the end of the month.

At $1,399, the Scrambler Core feels like a logical extension of Juiced’s rebooted lineup. You lose some battery, motor power, braking hardware, suspension travel, and a few mph compared to the Hardtail, but the underlying recipe is largely intact. For riders who mostly want the Scrambler look and feel – or parents shopping for a smaller rider – saving $300 may be a pretty compelling trade. Especially when you consider that the original Juiced Scrambler already led the industry in value for moto-style e-bikes from reputable brands.

Toss in the strong backing from Lectric and the 3-year warranty, and it’s hard to consider much else among the competition.

#4423. John F. Kennedy Jr.’s Last Car, a 1994 Saab 900 Coupe, Is Going Up for Auction

And, yes, in case you were wondering, it is a five-speed manual.

If you’ve ever wanted to own an automotive piece of Kennedy family history, now’s your chance. John F. Kennedy Jr.’s last car, a 1994 Saab 900 SE Coupe, will be auctioned off Wednesday, November 11th at 7 p.m. EST by RR Auctions.

The dark green three-door coupe was the last vehicle Kennedy owned before he, his wife Carolyn Bessette Kennedy, and sister-in-law Lauren Bessette were killed in a plane crash off the coast of Martha’s Vineyard on July 16, 1999. As he purchased it new, Kennedy was able to have the Saab fitted with a light beige leather interior, a five-speed manual transmission, and a turquoise-green “Main Beach” roof rack. There’s only 30,650 miles on the odometer, and RR Auctions says the vehicle shows evidence of age and use, including wear on the leather upholstery and areas of soiling on the carpeting. A printed photograph of John F. Kennedy Jr. and Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy beside the Saab will be included.

“For a man born into one of America’s wealthiest and most famous families, Kennedy’s choice of a Saab was notably modest. He purchased the new 900 SE from Zumbach Sports Cars in Manhattan in the summer of 1994 for $29,841.21, equipped with such everyday conveniences as a CD player and phone hookup,” the listing reads. “The practical Swedish hatchback suited the understated, slightly unconventional style Kennedy cultivated as an adult, far removed from the ostentation his wealth and celebrity could have afforded him. He drove it regularly around New York, and the intensely photographed nature of his life made the Saab a recurring backdrop to his final years: numerous period images show Kennedy, and later Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy, with the car, sometimes attempting to make their way through the paparazzi who followed them through the city.”

The Saab sat at the Larchmont, New York home of Kennedy’s friend, Kevin Hynes, for days after the plane crash. Hynes bought the Saab from the Kennedy estate in 2000 for $6000; in 2006, Hynes sold the 900 Coupe to Michael Esposito for $12,000.

When the vehicle was photographed on July 23, 1999, its contents included a football, a soccer ball, a rope, automotive fluid, a March 1999 issue of Rolling Stone, and a Piper baseball cap. Some of these items have been auctioned off previously, but this is the first time the vehicle itself has appeared. An E-ZPass transponder, a handwritten telephone-message sheet, an Airborne Express receipt associated with the 2000 estate transaction, and a DeWitt Stern Group envelope addressed to “Mr. John F. Kennedy” and marked “PERSONAL & CONFIDENTIAL” will be included with the purchase.

As of publication, 24 bids have been placed on the 1994 Saab 900. The current bidding price is $26,575.

#4421. Polestar’s Next EVs Will Borrow From This Gorgeous New Concept

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Polestar has unveiled a concept that makes you wish it would quietly slip into production tomorrow. The Formula 2030 is low, wide, and muscular, with four doors and enough suggested practicality to help you justify the rather large wheels.

Unfortunately, Polestar has no plans to produce the Formula 2030, but some of what you’re looking at is headed for cars you can actually buy. So this is the first Polestar penned under the brand’s new design boss, Philipp Römers, who took the role in August.

The study measures 184.3 inches (4,680 millimeters) in length and stands just 53.1 inches (1,350 mm) tall, making it lower than the Polestar 5. For reference, that’s about as low as Audi’s last TT sports car, but the concept’s aggressively bulging rear haunches and low stance make it look a lot meaner and sportier.

It features plenty of cool, subtle details you may not notice at first. The headlights, for instance, sit within a front aerodynamic wing, while a single upright windshield wiper screams motorsport. Polestar has ditched the familiar full-width rear lightbar for separate “Single Blade” lights. The 22-inch wheels, splitter, and diffuser sport variations of the same "Nitrogen" exterior color.

Inside, four individual seats have inflatable cushions and bolsters that adjust around their occupants. Rear-hinged rear doors swing open for pillarless access, while exposed structural components and flax-based composite seat backs really highlight the use of this sustainable material.

The coolest thing about the interior, though, is the fact that the cockpit also physically changes depending on the driving mode. Switch to Performance, and the 12.2-inch center screen lowers into the console while the steering wheel and its attached 20-inch driver display move closer. Choosing Autonomous mode moves the seat and wheel apart.

It features eight physical controls beneath the center screen. You can customize their functions and choose different hardware, including rocker switches or rotary controllers. After years of watching buttons disappear and get replaced by touchscreens, we’re happy to see real controls making a comeback.

Polestar doesn’t say how quick this concept is or how far it can go on one charge—this is purely a design showcase. However, a lot of what you’re seeing here will likely make its way into the upcoming Polestar 2 and its crossover cousin, the Polestar 7. The new 2 is scheduled for 2027 to replace a car that recently ended production after roughly 200,000 sales.

The Polestar 7 will follow a year later, with production planned at Volvo’s Košice plant in Slovakia, using Volvo technology, including cell-to-body battery construction and next-generation electric motors. Shared hardware should help contain costs, while Polestar promises its own driving character with more emphasis on sportiness and driving fun.

Those launches come as Polestar recorded little global growth. It reported 44,790 annual sales through September 2026, up just 0.6% over the same period of 2025. Its record third quarter brought 14,371 sales, but deliveries outside America fell 8%. American inventory sales helped keep the worldwide total positive.

But American sales won’t prop up the brand’s global total soon. Polestar cannot sell model year 2027 and newer vehicles in the United States under the Connected Vehicle Rule, although it can continue selling existing earlier-model inventory and supporting owners.

Europe is therefore now the priority, making the next 2 and European-built 7 especially important. The concept gives those cars an appealing visual direction, but their pricing, capabilities, and execution will determine whether that translates into stronger sales.

#4420. Garmin and Waze just teamed up on a clever new way to keep cyclists safer

Garmin and Waze are teaming up on an interesting new safety feature that could give cyclists a little extra protection when sharing the road with cars – by making cyclists themselves show up in Waze.

The new feature allows cyclists using a compatible Garmin Edge bike computer or Garmin smartwatch to share their location through Garmin’s LiveTrack feature. That location can then appear in real time to nearby drivers using Waze, with cyclists displayed as moving icons on the road.

As someone who recently joined the Garmin family myself with a smartwatch for tracking my cycling, running, and other activities, this is exactly the type of feature I love seeing added to the platform.

I’ve long maintained that safety – or more accurately, the perception that cycling isn’t safe – is one of the biggest impediments to getting more people onto bikes.

That’s especially true in the US, where cyclists are often forced to share roads with cars instead of enjoying the kind of widespread separated cycling infrastructure found in many more bike-friendly countries. And when a cyclist and a multi-ton vehicle have to occupy the same space, making sure the driver knows that cyclist is there can make a big difference.

Of course, an icon on Waze isn’t going to magically make cycling safe. It won’t replace protected bike lanes, better road design, slower vehicle speeds, or attentive drivers.

But I can certainly imagine situations where it could help. Riding at night or in poor visibility, approaching a blind curve, or simply traveling on a narrow road where a driver might otherwise come upon a cyclist unexpectedly are all situations where an advance warning could be useful.

The feature is opt-in through Garmin Connect and activates when the cyclist starts an outdoor cycling activity. Garmin says location sharing is temporary and session-based, and that cyclists’ personal information isn’t displayed in Waze. Of course, anyone who uses a personal GPS device has already accepted that their location is shared with Big Tech in exchange for features they value, but at least we know that any personalized info stays within Garmin instead of proliferating even further.

This is cool but requires both a Garmin product and the Waze app. IMHO better to equip new cars and trucks with bicycle and pedestrian detection.

Garmin LiveTrack itself is free for users with compatible Garmin devices and previously allowed cyclists to share their live location, speed, route, and other information with friends and family. I’ve used it myself as a safety feature when venturing off-road and on longer solo journeys. The Waze integration essentially expands that safety net to nearby motorists.

There’s obviously one big limitation: You need to be riding with a compatible Garmin device, and the driver needs to be using Waze.

But with Waze claiming around 200 million users globally and Garmin being one of the biggest names in cycling computers and fitness watches, that’s not exactly a tiny Venn diagram.

Anything that gives drivers another chance to see cyclists before actually seeing them sounds like a win to me.

#4418. The new BMW i3 just proved how efficient an EV can be after a nearly 3,700-mile road trip

Who says long EV road trips mean hours at charging stations? BMW drove the new i3 for over 3 days, covering nearly 3,700 miles, and it took less than 3 hours of charging.

BMW put the i3 to the ultimate test of efficiency, charging speed, and long-distance EV capability on a nearly 3,700-mile Pan-European journey.

The Paneurpeana, as it’s called, is considered the benchmark for range and charging speed. The route begins at the North Cape in Norway, the northernmost point of continental Europe you can reach by car, and ends in Tarifa, Spain, the southernmost point of mainland Europe.

BMW drove the new i3 50 xDrive for a total of 3,658 miles (5,886.7 km) across eight countries and spent just 2 hours, 45 minutes, and 54 seconds charging at an average of 275 kW.

The performance beat the previous record by more than seven hours, according to Mike Reichelt, head of BMW’s Neue Klasse

BMW said the charging points were not predetermined and that it had to account for external factors such as weather and traffic jams.

The new i3 was impressively efficient during the trip, consuming an average of just 12.5 kWh per 100 km, beating its official WLTP combined energy consumption of 18-13.4 kWh/100 km.

BMW said the trip took 3 days, 2 hours, and 41 minutes, with an average speed of 79.7 km/h, and that the i3 was charged exclusively at public charging points across national charging networks.

The vehicle was driven at all times by a single driver and was not modified in any way, in terms of hardware or software, from the standard i3 available for purchase.

BMW’s new i3 uses a 108.7 kWh battery and Gen6 eDrive system that provides a WLTP range of up to 566 miles (912 km).

With a drag coefficient of just 0.21, the new i3 is the most aerodynamically efficient BMW vehicle to date.

In the US, BMW said the new 2027 i3 50 xDrive will offer an EPA-estimated driving range of up to 468 miles.

With an 800V architecture, the electric sedan can add nearly 262 miles (423 km) of range (WLTP) in about 10 minutes at DC fast-charging speeds up to 400 kW. In the US, the i3 has a built-in NACS port.

Very reasonable. I've been with NK iX3 from Spain to Estonia and the experience is real - low consumption, great comfort and really fast charging. And there are more and more high speed chargers every month.

Like the new iX3, the i3 features BMW’s Neue Klasse interior design. The setup consists of BMW’s massive 43″ Panoramic Vision display that spans the base of the windshield and a 17.9″ floating central infotainment display.

The new BMW i3 50 xDrive is on sale in Germany starting at €65,900 with a WLTP range of up to 566 miles (912 km).

In the US, the 2027 BMW i3 50 xDrive and 2027 iX3 50 xDrive are available to order, both starting at $61,500.

#4417. Lucid's CEO Said The EV Startup 'Underinvested In Service.' Here's How It's Fixing That

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Getting a vehicle repaired is almost never pleasant, but Lucid is aiming to make things easier. Today, the direct-to-consumer luxury EV brand announced it is continuing to expand its network of brick-and-mortar service centers and is adding more mobile technicians to improve its after-sales support network. It says that the work it's already done decreased wait times by 20% in Q3 of this year, compared to the quarter before.

"We are building a broader, more accessible service network that supports our guests wherever they are in the ownership journey,” Billy Hayes, Lucid's new chief customer officer, said. “We are expanding our network, adding service personnel, and increasing Mobile Service capacity to reduce wait times and provide more convenient, responsive support."

The push comes as Lucid is gearing up to launch the first EVs on its midsize platform, more affordable cars that will be its first with true mainstream potential. The company says production will start in the second half of 2027. And a potential Model Y moment by way of the Earth and Cosmos—or so Lucid hopes—will necessitate a more robust service operation.

The effort to beef up service is part of a wide-ranging turnaround plan from new Lucid CEO Silvio Napoli, who took the reins of the EV startup this summer with a mission to cut costs and reduce losses. He's shaken up the carmaker's executive ranks, made deep cuts to staff, and slashed production at its Arizona factory to better balance supply with demand. (Lucid has struggled to grow sales of the Air and Gravity, which is a big part of the problem.)

He's focused the company on key areas such as robotaxi partnerships, the upcoming midsize vehicles, and improving the customer experience to help turn the tide. During his first earnings call as CEO in August, Napoli acknowledged that Lucid had "underinvested in service."

Currently, Lucid operates around 40 service centers across the U.S. to service its vehicles. Those who aren’t located near an in-person center have to make do with mobile servicing.

To improve customer service, Lucid has gone on a hiring and building spree. The company is building more service centers in North America, Europe, and the Middle East. And it's opening more locations that house a studio (a showroom where people can check out Lucids) alongside a service center. The first One just opened in Mission Viejo, California. Two more are set to open before the end of the year in LA and Dallas, and another is planned in Chicago for early 2027.

Lucid’s strategy goes beyond just building new locations, too. The company says it increased its technical and support staffing by over 40% globally since in Q3, as compared to Q2. It wants to increase that to 50% by the end of this year, and 60% by early 2027.

Mobile service is also growing. Lucid’s mobile service capacity is up 15% since Q2, while the company is targeting a 40% increase by the end of the year. Lucid says 20 new Gravity support vehicles are helping transport technicians to cars in need.

#4416. Toyota Revives the Scion Name on a Kei Truck for the U.S.

The defunct Scion brand is returning to experiment with new vehicle types, starting with a low-speed kei truck that you probably won't be able to buy.

Apparently, Toyota has been up at night watching Instagram reels. Reading the comments. Scratching its chin. Asking itself an important question: If people are already paying tariffs and other import fees to get old kei trucks into America from Japan, why don’t we just build new ones here?

That brings us to the Scion KEI-01. A small truck. With a tiny engine. And big dreams. What’s essentially a rebadged Daihatsu Hijet Jumbo, the Scion will instead be assembled at the same Toyota plant where the Grand Highlander and Sienna are built, in Princeton, Indiana. The word “kei” comes from the Japanese vehicle classification “keijidōsha,” which translates to light automobile.

See all results for used Toyota for sale near 92584

For now, you won’t find any hiding in the shadow of a lifted Toyota Tundra TRD Pro on dealer lots. Instead, these trucks—shorter than a Mazda MX-5 Miata—will be sold next year through a fleet-focused trial program to test the waters. If demand is strong, Toyota says limited retail sales could follow.

The Scion KEI-01 is as adorable as it looks and is said to weigh less than 2000 pounds, despite having all-wheel drive. Power comes from a tiny 660-cc three-cylinder engine paired with a continuously variable automatic transmission. It uses an independent front suspension, a solid rear axle, and a hydromechanical clutch to automatically shift power between the front and rear wheels based on traction needs. There’s also a “Lock” button to keep power evenly distributed between both axles.

The example Toyota showcased at a media event was equipped with tiny 145/80-12 Yokohama Super Van 355 tires. Its four-lug steel wheels, which almost hide the rear drum brakes, are roughly two inches smaller in diameter than the front brake rotors on the GR Corolla.

Here’s the catch. Just like another mini car—the Fiat Topolino—the Scion is restricted to low-speed duty, effectively making it a mullet-shaped golf cart. Top speed is limited to just 25 mph. Engineers tell us they baked this into the engine’s computer, and a simple “cut the wire” trick won’t unlock highway speeds. Its lack of speed is exactly how Toyota managed to get the KEI-01 into the U.S. so quickly. By meeting federal low-speed vehicle safety requirements, it can avoid the crash-test standards required of conventional passenger vehicles and pickups, retain its right-hand-drive layout, and stay as cute as a button.

See all results for used Toyota for sale near 92584

Measuring just over 11 feet long and less than five feet wide, the KEI-01 features a three-way folding cargo bed that can haul up to 600 pounds. That bed measures six feet six inches if you include the area under the cab, or five feet five inches without.

It comes with air conditioning, reclining seats, and push-button ignition. It will be sold with a cab-mounted reverse camera and may offer a towing package as optional equipment. Yes, it’s got airbags, though not many. Full pricing and options are still very TBD, as production is slated to begin in mid 2027.

The future of the Scion brand has also begun to take shape as a “freedom lab.” Toyota is using the name not as a conventional reboot, but as an outlet for experimental mobility ideas, such as a truck that measures just 11 feet in length.

Alongside the KEI-01, Toyota showed off its SxS Concept (previously revealed at SEMA last year), a side-by-side off-roader packing a turbocharged hybrid inline-four engine with more than 300 horsepower, and the BKE Concept scooter that already looks leagues more comfortable to ride than Honda’s Motocompacto.

It might not initially look like it, but the KEI-01 fits rather comfortably as a Scion. The original Scion brand spent its first life trying to convince young people to buy Toyotas. They wanted people to swap wheels, add racing stripes, and personalize an affordable car. That’s exactly what many people already do with their kei trucks. Just ask the guy baking wood-fired pizzas from the back of his Subaru Sambar if tiny trucks are any fun.

#4415. 10 Details That Show Rockstar Went Above and Beyond With GTA VI

Aden Carter is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2020. He specializes in lists and guides, with a focus on RPGs, horror games, survival horror, Soulslikes, cozy/sim games, and action-adventure titles. Before joining DualShockers, Aden contributed to GameRant, XDA, Gamepur, I

Rockstar has made some amazing games over the years, and one thing that always remains the same is that the team has an amazing attention to detail. The maps are massive, full of life, have tons of activities, and even have insane levels of detail that you would never even think to look at.

A small instance of this can be seen in Arthur Morgan, as his hair grows, can be cut, and even styled. It is easy to see why Rockstar often gets praise from gamers. However, now it is time for GTA VI to shine.

Like before, Rockstar has definitely gone above and beyond with the attention to detail, and this is just part of the reason why GTA VI is a great game.

Ah yes, just when I am trying to get any work done, I turn to my phone, pick it up, and start flipping through social media. Specifically, I start swiping through shorts on YouTube or reels on Instagram.

If you are addicted to doomscrolling through life like many people in the world, the good news is that you can do that in GTA VI. Rockstar has never shied away from emulating life in some aspects of each of their games, and this time, you can use the Snapmatic app in GTA VI to scroll through posts and viral clips.

Of course, this has a connection to the actual gameplay, and no, you can’t become a viral star in GTA VI, but it does show the level of detail Rockstar is going for in the game, as the feed gets updated. Just don’t doomscroll very long.

The wanted system has evolved over the years that the Grand Theft Auto series has existed, but it has never been this detailed. Previously, if you became wanted, you could simply hide, wait out the cops, and leave when they forget you exist.

Now, the cops remember you. They know what you look like, whether you were with a partner, what car you drive, and the clothes you wear. Each of these gets marked, and you need to take care of them if you want to avoid detection.

If they know your outfit, you need to change. If they know your car, you need to get a new one. If you don’t wear a mask, they will know your face. It is a level of detail never seen in the wanted system.

Grand Theft Auto V had a decent number of buildings you could enter, with the total being roughly around 100. Still, when you are living in a city, that number is pretty small and mostly impressive by game standards.

Grand Theft Auto VI takes this to a new level, and it shows how dedicated Rockstar is to going above and beyond with detail, as it is estimated that 70% of the buildings are enterable. The confirmed number by the mapping community based on trailers and available data is sitting at around 400, that is already over four times the number in the previous game.

It is amazing that Rockstar has taken the time and energy to put in so many details and fully flesh out all of these buildings.

GTA Online 2.0 will be coming eventually, and there are some changes that Rockstar should make.

Leonida is based on Florida, and if you have ever been to Florida, you know that there is a lot of wildlife there. Venture outside of the city, and you can find numerous animals living in the wetlands.

Rockstar made sure to go above and beyond when it comes to the game’s animals with the team putting in more than 170 different animal species. This includes over 60 bird species, 30 land mammals, and also various aquatic life and reptiles.

For context, Grand Theft Auto V has around 28 different animal species, and Red Dead Redemption 2 has over 200. Leonida will be just as wild as the real Florida.

The Grand Theft Auto series obviously has a large emphasis on committing crimes, with each game giving you the ability to rob stores, steal cars, and more. However, none of the previous titles have the same level of detail when it comes to committing a crime.

GTA VI has multiple options when committing a crime. Will you wear a mask? Do you want to bring a partner? Are you going to use a silencer on your weapon? This all plays into whether you get caught in the act and how the police respond.

On top of this, other crimes like stealing a car are now more detailed as well, with you having the ability to bust windows or even use tools to pop locks. Some cars even have trackers. You can even use an app to determine a car’s resale value.

It is easy to overlook NPCs in a video game unless you are directly interacting with them. All the people on the street tend to blur together at times, but when you stop to take a look, you will see various NPCs that look alike.

In GTA V, it is estimated that there are around 800 unique NPCs roaming the streets of Los Santos and beyond. However, when tested, players have shown it doesn’t take very long to run into the same NPC but in a different location.

Let’s scale this up to GTA VI. There isn’t an official number yet, but Rockstar has stated that the NPCs will be far more diverse, with they varying in height and weight. They will also have defining details like birthmarks, moles, skin conditions, and more. Even the sizes of their muscles, butts, and chests can differ. That’s a lot of detail.

The weather often gets crazy down in Florida. It is normal for residents of the state to deal with torrential downpours, strong winds, tropical storms, and even hurricanes. In other words, you can’t expect Leonida to not have similar weather.

GameInformer detailed some of the weather effects that will be in GTA VI, and according to them, there will be tropical storms and hurricanes that make “water gush off roof edges and lamposts,” and make it so “everything is dripping wet.”

This means that you will need to unleash your inner Florida Man and run through a hurricane to see what happens. Maybe you will get tossed around. I just hope Rockstar captured the downpour that seems to happen every day around 3pm.

GTA 6 features a completely rebuilt dynamic wind and atmospheric system designed to bring the tropical world of Leonida to life like never before.

Being a Rockstar game, there is a degree of change that can be expected to happen to your character. This didn’t exist in GTA V, but in Red Dead Redemption 2, Arthur Morgan’s weight could change, his hair could grow and be cut, and his face changes.

Rockstar has taken this a step further for GTA VI, as you have two protagonists, and both of them can have their appearance change over time. Overeating causes weight gain, undereating causes weight loss, working out makes your muscles grow, and much more.

The protagonists aren’t just static characters that don’t change with time, they evolve and grow. Their hair also grows and needs to be cut. This level of detail is above and beyond what happens in a normal game.

While GTA V is great, the NPCs in that game are pretty lackluster. When you commit a crime, they mostly switch between two actions; fight or run. Mostly, they run away from guns, car crashes, or whatever else.

The NPCs in GTA VI, however, act much differently. They are more lifelike. They will take out their phones to record you. You can listen in on conversations, and the NPCs will get angry if they spot you. The NPCs will go so far as to remember you.

This means that if you continuously wreak havoc in Leonida, the NPCs will act differently towards you. Some may even be hostile as soon as they see you. A lot of work goes into making NPCs feel lifelike, and Rockstar is going above and beyond with it.

If it wasn’t obvious already, GTA VI is about a couple named Lucia and Jason. The pair are trying to create a better life and get out of crime. A big part of the game revolves around their relationship.

The couple can spend time together, furthering their bond. They can play games like mini-golf, go scuba diving together, and much more. The more they spend time together, the stronger their bond will become.

Rockstar put a lot of detail in just the relationship aspect of the game, with your partner messaging you throughout the day to check in and more. You actually need to care about who you commit crime with, as if you don’t your relationship will fail and affect the story.

The Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks have revealed some interesting details about the game, such as new mechanics and changes to the menus.

#4413. Mercedes’ EV Charging Network Hit 100 Locations After 3 Years In The U.S.

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Mercedes-Benz may have sold its EV charging network in Europe, but the automaker’s American network is still alive and well, and it’s now celebrating its third anniversary.

Since debuting in November 2023, the Mercedes-Benz High-Powered Charging (MB HPC) network has gone from just a handful of locations in a few states to nearly 1,000 individual ports at 100 sites across 28 U.S. states and Canada's British Columbia.

Mercedes-Benz High-Power Charging station in Ashburn, VA

All of the carmaker’s fast chargers can deliver up to 400 kilowatts of power, with over 245,000 customers topping up their EVs at a Mercedes-Benz stall in the past three years. According to the company, the vast majority of stalls have both CCS and NACS connectors, while only 7% of locations have just CCS connectors.

That’s a big thing nowadays, when most of the new EVs on the market have a Tesla-style NACS charging port. The smaller inlet started making a splash among traditional automakers after Ford broke industry barriers and convinced Tesla to open up its Supercharger network to other makes. That said, NACS-equipped vehicles can still charge at CCS stations with an adapter, and vice versa.

Near-perfect uptime has been a headlining feature of Mercedes-Benz’s charging network stateside since its launch, but while those figures have remained relatively unchanged in the past three years, another metric has emerged as a differentiator, at least in the German automaker’s eyes.

Mercedes-Benz Charging Hub at the headquarters of Mercedes-Benz USA in Sandy Springs, Georgia

The first-time success rate, which measures charging sessions that start on the first try, has become the company’s “guiding star.” Back in 2023, it stood at roughly 84%, meaning that about one and a half sessions out of ten didn’t work on the first attempt. Now, three years later, the first-time success rate has climbed to over 90%.

Mercedes’ EV charging network in the U.S. uses 400-kilowatt dispensers exclusively, mostly from Alpitronic, and the stations are usually located at or around premium shopping locations. According to DCFC Tracker, the largest MB HPC site has 20 stalls and is located in Orlando, Florida. The company’s smallest operations, in Conyers, Georgia, and Red Bluff, California, have four stalls each.

All locations have credit card readers, but EV drivers can also use various charging apps to pay for sessions, as well as an RFID card issued by Mercedes-Benz dealers. Plug & Charge is also supported. Pricing varies between $0.35/kilowatt-hour and $0.60/kWh, depending on location, and a $25 pre-authorization fee is temporarily held to verify available funds. After the session ends, drivers will be charged the actual amount based on the energy used, and the rest will be released.

Last month, Mercedes-Benz High-Power Charging North America appointed Madeline Ebert as its new CEO.

Updated to reflect that the charging network has delivered over one million sessions since 2023, and that the percentage of CCS-only stalls is 7%.

#4411. Lucid's $50,000 Tesla Model Y Rival Is Getting Closer To Production. Here's The Latest

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Lucid is on track to start producing the Cosmos crossover in the second half of 2027, the California EV startup said in its third quarter earnings call on Monday. The electric crossover will rival the Tesla Model Y and Rivian R2 when it goes on sale and is a "must-win" project for the company, according to new CEO Silvio Napoli.

This week, Lucid provided a few updates on the status of its most important model to date. Here's what we learned.

Lucid is a small player in the EV market, but it has big ambitions. Its third quarter sales plunged to only 3,806 vehicles. However, its January-to-September sales are up 33% thanks to more Gravity SUVs reaching customers. It is now trying to prove it can transition from a niche luxury EV maker into a profitable high-volume carmaker.

The upcoming midsize platform and the EVs that it will underpin is central to that strategy. And progress on the AMP-2 manufacturing plant where production will kick off is coming along, Napoli said.

“AMP-2 is moving towards inauguration and production readiness, and Midsize is now on track,” Napoli said. The company’s second manufacturing plant—and first international one—is located in King Abdullah Economic City, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. The plant already assembles the Lucid Air sedan, which is also produced at its AMP-1 plant in Casa Grande, Arizona.

“Stamping line installation is complete, and commissioning is underway,” Napoli said. “Body shop installation is accelerating. Drive unit installation is progressing and paint is now in finalization with equipment continuing to arrive on site."

The Cosmos was originally scheduled to launch by the end of this year, but Napoli pushed it to 2027 amid a broader turnaround plan. The company said it won’t rush the new EV to the market to avoid the same quality issues faced by the Gravity and Air.

Lucid also indicated that the Cosmos itself is getting closer to its final production form.

"The final stage of prototyping is underway including homologation and crash testing. Pilot production in Coolidge is entering its final build phase, including know-how transfer to AMP-2," Napoli said on Monday. Apparent Cosmos prototypes have been spotted near Lucid facilities.

Lucid said this week that it plans to announce reveal and production-start timelines in the first quarter of next year.

We already know a lot about the Cosmos. It will start at around $50,000. Napoli told CNN in August that it will have more than 400 miles of range. At its Investor Day in March, the company said it will get both nickel-manganese-cobalt (NMC) and lithium-iron-phosphate (LFP) batteries.

I also saw a prototype behind closed doors and it looks like a baby Gravity. Inside, a massive touchscreen spans the width of the dashboard. It will get a centralized architecture that’s more powerful and costs less to build, along with an 800-volt platform. It will be powered by one of the most energy dense and compact drive units in the industry, called Atlas.

The startup is also planning to roll out tens of thousands of robotaxis through its partnership with Uber and Nuro in the U.S. and Bolt in Europe. Those will include both the Gravity (U.S.) and a midsize EV (For U.S. and Europe). The company is also on track to roll out the first Gravity SUVs in the Bay Area in the first quarter of 2027. (The original timeline was end of 2026.)

To help pull this all off, the company announced that it had received an additional $1.75 billion loan from Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, which is also its majority owner.

#4410. BYD and Geely approached FIA about a 12th F1 team, says Ben Sulayem

BYD and Geely have both approached the FIA about entering Formula 1, the sport’s governing body confirmed. FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem named the two Chinese automakers while speaking at the New Economy Forum in Madrid, as first reported by Grande Prêmio.

But there’s no open process for a 12th team, and neither company has a deal. The FIA is also pushing F1 toward the kind of engine an EV maker has the least reason to build.

“One of them was BYD and another was Geely,” Ben Sulayem said of the manufacturers that have reached out about joining the grid.

He said he suggested that BYD buy an existing team instead of starting a new one. BYD wasn’t interested in that route. It wants its own team, so Ben Sulayem told the company to come back with a “serious proposal” that shows the project can work.

He also made it clear that Chinese manufacturers won’t get special treatment. Any bid would go through the same process as other prospective entrants, and the rules won’t be rewritten to suit them. Right now, there’s no expansion process at all: the FIA isn’t actively looking for a 12th team.

Still, Ben Sulayem repeated that he’d like F1’s next newcomer to come from China, pointing to the country’s EV technology and the Chinese Grand Prix in Shanghai.

This isn’t new for BYD. Back in March, we reported that BYD was exploring a Formula 1 entry, either by buying a team or building one from scratch.

In April, executive vice president Stella Li said BYD had met F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali in Shanghai and that an entry was “something we’re discussing.” By July, the tone had cooled. Li said “the dream is always there, but we don’t have a concrete agenda,” and special advisor Alfredo Altavilla set a clear condition: “We will never participate in Formula 1 just to put a sticker on the side of a car.”

Altavilla said BYD would only consider F1 to the extent its technology can serve the sport.

Geely is the new name here. The group sold 3.02 million vehicles last year and owns Volvo, Polestar, and Lotus, a brand with decades of F1 history. It’s also heading into Canada next year as Chinese automakers push hard into new markets.

The last newcomer, Cadillac, took a long road. The FIA opened an expression-of-interest process in 2023, and GM’s team only joined the grid as the 11th team this season, running Ferrari power until its own power unit arrives. Audi got in the other way, by taking over Sauber.

Here’s where it gets awkward for an EV maker. The 2026 F1 power units split output roughly 50/50 between the combustion engine and electric power, with the MGU-K jumping to 350 kW.

The FIA is already walking that back. In June, it agreed to shift the split to 60-40 in favor of combustion for 2027 and 2028. And Ben Sulayem has been pushing for V8 engines running on sustainable fuel with “minor electrification” for the next rules cycle, starting in 2031 at the latest, possibly 2030. Domenicali says F1 should have a package ready to discuss by the end of this year.

So the FIA president wants a Chinese EV maker on the grid, while pushing a rulebook that makes their main strength less relevant.

We like the idea of BYD or Geely in F1. Chinese automakers have the money and the engineers, and they badly need brand prestige outside China. BYD in particular has been on a performance push with Yangwang, and F1 would be the loudest possible way to tell Europe it’s not just a cheap car brand.

This "EV or no EV" discussion in F1 is becoming absurd. F1 bills itself as the technological pinnacle of motor sport, but then it tries to limit the racing to specific engine types and sizes in a way that defies that concept of modern technology. This year, that has meant cars that decide for themselves how much power to generate rather than allowing the driver to control the car - a system that violates F1's own rules.

F1 has the cost cap to keep expenses on technology under control, and no one would question safety rules like having enough battery left at the end of the race to avoid stopping in the middle of the track (like F1 does with requiring an amount of fuel left at the end of the race), or battery safety requirements to prevent explosive fires and the like. Other than that, why not let the companies decide for themselves?

But Ben Sulayem’s comments don’t move things much. There’s no entry process, BYD has already turned down his main suggestion, and Geely’s interest is a name dropped at a conference, not a bid.

A Chinese would likely be good for F1 as well. Motorsports are on the rise in China, and that would be the cherry on top in helping popularize the sport in the world’s largest market.

The bigger issue is the engine. Altavilla was clear that BYD isn’t interested in slapping a logo on a car. It wants F1 to showcase its technology, and BYD’s technology is batteries and electric drive. The FIA’s V8 push goes the other way. It’s hard to sell an EV giant on a sport that’s reducing the electric part of the powertrain.

If you’re following how fast EV tech is moving, from BYD’s batteries to F1’s hybrid power units, you can put some of that tech to work at home: pairing an EV with rooftop solar can cut your driving costs to nearly zero. #4409. Rockstar to Host Grand Theft Auto 6 Launch Festival in Miami

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

We are exactly 10 days out from the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, and I can feel the boundaries of reality straining and groaning in anticipation. This game’s launch is slated to be so colossal, so era-defining, that analysts have already predicted the U.S. economy will lose a billion dollars in productivity costs due to everyone calling out sick. It’s the game that nearly every other game was too scared to launch in November because of.

It’s kind of fitting that such an apocalyptic-level release would be accompanied by a bout of mad revelry, and if there’s one thing that Rockstar has proven itself particularly good at, it’s running equally massive real-life advertising campaigns. To that end, the company has announced that, on November 21, a couple of days after release proper, a launch festival will be held on the shores of Miami, Florida.

Rockstar says GTA 6 pre-loading begins November 10 and could require up to 212 GB, though some official pages still show the old date.

Ticket sales will be exclusively by a lottery, so assuming you’re not too busy that weekend actually playing the game, you may have a chance to join in on a generation-defining party, slated to feature a swath of some of the biggest names in modern music.

The event is officially titled “Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival,” and is being jointly hosted by both Rockstar itself and PlayStation, as well as produced by the creators of the Ill Points music festival. According to the official website, the event will be a “one-of-a-kind launch event that features two stages of nonstop music,” held at the Mana Wynwood in Miami.

The participating artists include many of those whose tracks are featured on the official Grand Theft Auto 6 soundtrack, including, but very much not limited to, Cactus Jack presents Travis Scott, Don Toliver, Kodak Black, Sofaygo, and Cardi B.

The event will be a “one-of-a-kind launch event that features two stages of nonstop music."

The event will only be open to those ages 17 and up, with valid photo ID required for entrance and confirmation that you’re at least 21 for consumption of alcohol. Ticket sales will be handled by DICE via exclusive codes distributed by Laylo. These codes will be distributed via lottery; entries into this lottery are currently open, and will close on Tuesday, November 10 at 4:00 PM eastern time, with the winners drawn that same day at 7:00 PM.

Grand Theft Auto 6's Burger Shot and Cluckin' Bell are taking over Miami Heat games.

Once the winners are selected, actual ticket sales will open on Wednesday, November 11 at 12 PM eastern. Codes are single-use and non-transferable, and tickets are limited to two-per-code. The official site doesn’t specify how much tickets will cost, but much like the game itself, don’t expect them to be cheap.

Even putting aside its efforts throughout the past year to drip-feed details about Grand Theft Auto 6’s release, Rockstar has been truly pulling out all the stops to maintain a constant presence in the public consciousness.

One amusing example of this has been the game’s recurring presence in the current season of South Park, throughout which characters have remarked variations of, “everything is gonna change in November. Y’know, when Grand Theft Auto 6 comes out.” This, of course, was a cheeky nod to the recent United States Midterm elections, though in the most recent episode, Rockstar actually sent the show’s creators exclusive footage of the game, which was showcased during the episode.

Rockstar also ran a takeover event of the Selfridges department store in London, with the Oxford Street London Corner Shop being done up in Vice City iconography and colors and selling a swath of GTA 6-themed apparel and accessories, some of which was priced in the thousands of Pounds. There was even a custom Ferrari parked inside the store right by the street window for all to see.

As Rockstar Games has taken its marketing efforts to Miami, lawmakers have expressed divided opinions on how the campaign impacts the real-life city.

#4408. Polestar’s Formula 2030 Concept Car Is a Futuristic Look at Tactile Driving

The concept previews the brand’s next-gen designs, which will influence new production cars in the next two years.

Polestar revealed a Formula 2030 concept car at a media drive event for the Polestar 4, and while it’s not headed for production, the electric carmaker says some of its design language will preview the next-generation Polestar 2 as well as the upcoming Polestar 7. The four-door concept has a rear hatch and is unmistakably Polestar, as evident by the brand’s signature “Dual Blade” headlights and minimalistic design. However, its low-slung profile and flared rear fenders give it an aggressive, performance-oriented silhouette.

See all results for used Polestar for sale near 30530

The car’s coach doors remove the need for a B-pillar, and the A-pillar is disguised to give the windshield and windows a wrap-around effect. Interestingly, the concept has a single windshield wiper. Glass replaces a traditional roof, and the trunk gets a large window—a stark deviation from some of Polestar’s other windowless rear ends. The trunk’s floor is also transparent, and race-inspired Öhlins dampers peek through underneath.

Polestar calls the concept’s rear end “UFO-esque.” And instead of the single long light bar that angles downward on previous models, the concept car’s lighting signature is more subtle, with just two thin taillights located under the trunk.

Nitrogen, a new exterior color that debuts on the Formula 2030 concept, shows up in three different finishes around the exterior. Polestar’s tone-in-tone treatment uses a mix of glossy, matte, and satin finishes to distinguish details like the side cladding and aero bits. Even the 22-inch wheels are color-matched, with Swedish Gold-colored Brembo brake calipers as an accent.

Inside, the four-seater continues the tone-in-tone color scheme with light-colored upholstery and gold accents in the seatbelts and controls. The seats feature inflatable bolsters and cushions that mold themselves to each occupant, and most of the interior is composed of recycled materials.

Two screens—one attached to the steering column and one in the center of the dashboard—angle toward the driver, and eight physical controls lie in the center console below the larger screen. Drivers have options for each of the controls, both in what kind of tactile control it is, like a rocker switch or dial, and what function it affects.

The center console also houses a drive-mode selector where drivers can choose between Performance, Normal, and Autonomous modes. In Performance mode, the center screen lowers to sit flush with the center console while the steering wheel and gauge screen move closer to the driver. In Autonomous mode, the car’s concealed lidar unit appears outside the car while the steering wheel and driver’s seat move further apart inside the cabin.

See all results for used Polestar for sale near 30530

The concept car wasn’t built to reach production, but Polestar has already confirmed that some of its elements will show up in the next-generation Polestar 2, which is slated to arrive in early 2027, and the upcoming Polestar 7, which is expected to arrive in 2028. Polestar is now banned from selling new vehicles in the United States, so you’ll have to head across the Atlantic to actually get your hands on Polestar’s upcoming lineup.

#4407. Watch BYD’s robotic charging arm plug itself in and charge EVs in 5 minutes [Video]

BYD’s Flash Charging tech can charge an EV in as little as five minutes. Now, BYD is taking things a step further with integrated solar power and a robotic arm that plugs itself in. See how it all works in action.

After unveiling the Yangwang Altior in the UAE on Monday, its new ultra-luxury flagship electric sedan, BYD showcased its latest breakthrough technology.

The Chinese automaker launched a new integrated charging system in the Abu Dhabi desert that brings BYD’s “Three Green Dreams” to life.

In 2006, BYD president and CEO Wang Chuanfu revealed his vision of “Three Green Dreams,” including harnessing solar power to generate renewable energy, storing that energy in batteries, and replacing gas-powered vehicles with electric ones that run on clean energy.

The new charging system is the “world’s first,” according to BYD, to integrate solar power generation, energy storage, Flash Charging, and robotic charging together in one solution.

BYD’s Flash Charging tech enables a vehicle’s battery to charge from 10% to 70% in five minutes, essentially the same time it takes to fill up at a gas station. For a full recharge, or to go from 10% to 97%, it takes just nine minutes.

The new robotic charging arm automatically locates the vehicle’s charging port, opens its cover, plugs in, and then removes it once the session is over.

By combining robotic charging with its Automated Valet Parking, BYD said the new tech goes beyond automated driving and parking to the charging process itself.

Once the vehicle is parked, the robotic charging arm automatically takes over and connects it to Flash Charging without the driver even touching the cable.

A post shared by Michael Martinez (@mmichael_martinez)

Michaël Martinez, head of marketing at BYD France, posted a video (shown above) showcasing the new charging tech in action.

The integrated solution is built around BYD’s Solar-Storage-Charging (SSC) system, fusing solar energy generation, battery storage, and its 5-minute Flash Charging tech. Together, the setup captures energy from the sun, stores it, and distributes it as needed.

If they could tie this into a smart summon type of capability, where the vehicle communicates with the charger and moves the vehicle into the proper location for charging and then moves to a parking spot once charging is complete. Rental car fleets would benefit and so would those in shopping centers. There are so many possibilities and this looks far more mature that the old snake charging Tesla demoed.

BYD has over 16 years of experience in the solar industry with a portfolio that includes solar cells, modules, and systems.

Its solar division, BYD Solar, does business in over 100 countries and regions. By using solar power, BYD said, the SCC system can operate independently off-the-grid.

The new technology is part of BYD’s wider Flash Charging rollout. By the end of 2027, the company plans to deploy 6,000 Flash Charging stations globally.

#4406. This Mercedes Went 539 Miles On A Charge. Is Range Anxiety Finally Dead?

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

A 2027 Mercedes-Benz EQS sedan just traveled well over 500 miles in a real-world range test by Edmunds. It's an amazing result that shows range anxiety may finally be fading into the rearview—especially if you've got deep enough pockets.

When put through its paces, the Mercedes EQS 450+ covered 539 miles, surpassing its 467-mile EPA rating by a substantial 72 miles. That also makes it the longest-range sedan Edmunds has ever tested, beating out the Lucid Air Dream Edition by 34 miles. Keep in mind that Edmunds tests range on a route with a 60/40 split between city and highway driving, whereas the EPA aims for a 55/45 breakdown. In Edmunds' testing, only the Cadillac Escalade IQ has bested the EQS 450+’s range, covering a stunning 558 miles.

For 2027, Mercedes-Benz updated the EQS with some tweaks that helped boost its efficiency and range. The battery is now 122 kilowatt-hours, up from 118 kWh in the older model. The rear motor now has a two-speed transmission, and the whole platform has been upgraded to an 800-volt design. These upgrades already boosted the EQS’s stated range on paper. Overdelivering in the real world confirms that the range anxiety argument against EVs is only getting harder to make.

The EQS can't just drive farther than its predecessor. The updated 800-volt platform allows it to charge far more quickly.

Because of its long range, stellar efficiency, and strong DC fast-charging rate, Edmunds says it’s the third-fastest charging EV it has ever tested based on its miles-per-hour charging metric. The EQS 450+ was able to add 100 miles of range in just 7 minutes is only bested by the Hyundai Ioniq 6 and the new Mercedes-Benz CLA 250+. The CLA 250+ also has some of the same tricks that the EQS 450+ uses to increase efficiency and lower charging times, like a two-speed transmission and an 800-volt platform.

To be sure, Edmunds’ test example stickered at nearly $122,000, which isn’t attainable for most EV buyers. Still, the growing availability of ultra-long-range EVs shows that range anxiety is becoming a thing of the past. A new generation of luxury EVs is proving that out; the BMW iX3, i3, and iX5 all have range ratings well north of 400 miles, while the Volvo EX60 and Porsche Cayenne Electric land around there too. For its part, Edmunds has now tested six EVs that sail past 500 miles.

What may be even more encouraging is that there plenty of 300-mile cars on offer too, and many of those won't break the bank like a six-figure Mercedes. Edmunds says more than 90 models have exceeded 300 miles in its testing.

Ten years ago, 300 miles seemed like a stretch goal for the mainstream; only the Model S had such a rating. Now, it’s not hard to find cars like the Chevy Equinox EV or Kia EV3 that can easily hit that number, for prices that aren’t too far off from the average gas-powered crossover.

EVs still have obstacles to overcome in the eyes of the general public, like high purchase prices, scattered charging infrastructure, and a lack of options. But increasingly, range isn't one of them.
